faqJsonLd.question: Are speaker notes invisible on Zoom?
faqJsonLd.answer: Yes. The CueCard window is left out of screen capture by the operating system, so Zoom sends everyone your slides and never your notes, even though the window is right there on your screen. Try one practice share first to see it for yourself.

faqJsonLd.question: How do I use speaker notes in Zoom meetings?
faqJsonLd.answer: Install CueCard for Mac or Windows, paste your notes in or sync them from Google Slides, then start your Zoom call as usual. Your notes sit on your screen where you can read them, and stay out of what you share.

faqJsonLd.question: Can I sync Google Slides notes for Zoom presentations?
faqJsonLd.answer: Yes. Install the CueCard browser extension alongside the app, and the speaker notes for the slide you are on appear in CueCard and change as you move through the deck. Google Slides is optional, though — paste your notes straight in and CueCard works with any deck, or with none at all.

faqJsonLd.question: Do I need anything besides the CueCard app?
faqJsonLd.answer: Yes, one more thing: the CueCard browser extension. The app is the window your notes appear in, and the extension is what reads the notes out of your deck and sends them across. Google Slides needs both, and both are free.

faqJsonLd.question: Do notes update automatically when I change slides?
faqJsonLd.answer: Yes. Move to the next slide and CueCard shows that slide's speaker notes. You never have to scroll or click across to keep the two in step.

faqJsonLd.question: Which browsers support the Google Slides extension?
faqJsonLd.answer: Chrome, Firefox and Safari. The Chrome extension also covers Edge, Brave and Arc, and the Safari one is installed for you by the Mac app.
